en.question: Support tickets arrive as refund requests, technical faults, or billing questions, and each type needs very different handling and a different prompt. Which pattern fits?

options.text: Parallelisation: run all three specialised handlers and merge their answers.
options.note: Running all three wastes spend and produces two irrelevant answers to reconcile.

options.text: Routing: classify the ticket first, then dispatch to the matching handler.
Evaluator-optimiser: generate an answer, then critique and revise in a loop.
options.note: That pattern refines a single output; it does not select a handler.

options.text: A single prompt that contains all three sets of handling instructions.
options.note: A combined prompt is longer, more confusing, and degrades every category.

en.explanation: Routing exists for distinct input categories needing separate treatment. Classifying first lets each path use a focused prompt and an appropriately sized model instead of one bloated prompt covering every case.
